subject: general
question:
Identify the product (P) in the following reaction:

Limestone (s) → P + CO₂ (g)
solution:
The correct answer is __**CaO(s).**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• Limestone naturally contains **calcium carbonate**.
 
• When limestone is heated strongly, the calcium carbonate that it contains endothermically **absorbs heat**, breaking down to generate** calcium oxide.**
 
• As the limestone is heated, an **orange light** **serves **as a sign of this.
 
• **Calcium carbonate **is created from **carbon dioxide **and **calcium oxide**.
 
• **CaCO3(s) → CaO(s) + CO2(g)**
 
• A crucial component in the creation of **cement **and some varieties of **plaster **is calcium oxide, sometimes referred to as **quicklime**. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• From the crust of the Earth, limestone, a sedimentary rock, is a rich resource.
 
• It can be put to a lot of different uses:
 
 
• It is a **building material **that is usable.
 
• By combining **heated clay **and **powdered limestone**, it is used to make **cement**.
 
• It is a key component of **toothpaste**.
 
• It can be added to **meals **as a **supplement **to supply calcium ions for healthy bones and teeth.
 
• It is a useful **raw material **that can be processed for use in the **chemical industry**.
 
• It can be utilised to **balance acidic soil **so that plants can grow more successfully.
